subject: Oceanography
title: Deep-Sea Mining
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Deep-Sea Mining.

hook.text: The deep seafloor holds trillions of dollars in metals—manganese nodules, cobalt crusts, and sulfide deposits.

buildup.text: Polymetallic nodules litter abyssal plains—potato-sized lumps rich in manganese, nickel, copper, and cobalt.

discovery.text: These metals are essential for batteries and electronics—demand is surging with the green energy transition.

twist.text: Mining would destroy seafloor ecosystems that took millions of years to develop—and may never recover.

climax.text: The International Seabed Authority is debating regulations—but environmental groups want a moratorium.

punchline.text: The metals we need for a green future lie in the last untouched wilderness.

quiz.question: What are polymetallic nodules?
options: Metal-rich lumps on the deep seafloor
